Ansonia.QN: 1.  "Shall Section 43 of the City of Ansonia Charter be amended to require that the Mayor submit a proposed fiscal-year budget to the Board of Apportionment and Taxation no later than the second Monday in March each year and if a public referendum is necessary shall the timeline for the public referendum be changed to no more than fourteen calendar days and no less than ten calendar days after approval by the Board of Aldermen?"

2.  "Shall a public referendum be held on the budget for the City of Ansonia whenever the Board of Aldermen approves a budget that increases total expenditures by 4% or more compared to the prior fiscal year?"

3.  "Shall Section 129 of the City of Ansonia Charter be amended to replace references to the Fire Superintendent with Fire Chief, establish the process for selecting the second Fire Chief, and specify the appointing authority for members of the Board of Fire Commissioners?"
4.  "Shall Section 130 of the City of Ansonia Charter be eliminated as the Superintendent of Fire Alarms be obsolete?"

Burlington.QN: 1.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $5,000,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for HVAC replacements and improvements at district schools?"

2.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $14,935,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for roof replacements and improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School, Lake Garda School and Har-Bur Middle School?"

3.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $3,900,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for the installation of a multipurpose synthetic turf field and related improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School?"

4.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $3,100,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for the installation of a multipurpose engineered natural grass field and related improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School?"

Cheshire.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Cheshire appropriate $1,100,000 for a replacement salt shed at the Public Works Garage and authorize the issue of $1,100,000 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation, the amount of such bonds and notes to be reduced by the amount of project grants received?"

2.  "Shall the Town of Cheshire appropriate $2,350,000 for the Road Improvement Program and authorize the issue of $2,350,000 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation, the amount of such bonds and notes to be reduced by the amount of project grants received?"

3.  "Shall the Town of Cheshire appropriate $1,375,000 for road reconstruction of Dickerman Road and authorize the issue of $1,375,000 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation, the amount of such bonds and notes to be reduced by the amount of project grants received?"

4.  "Shall the Town of Cheshire appropriate $1,000,000 for acquisition of land for recreational, open space, conservation, educational and/or municipal purposes and authorize the issue of $1,000,000 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation, the amount of such bonds and notes to be reduced by the amount of project grants received?"

5.  "Shall the Town of Cheshire appropriate $875,000 for safety and drainage improvements to the loading dock area at Cheshire High School and authorize the issue of $875,000 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation, the amount of such bonds and notes to be reduced by the amount of project grants received?"

Clinton.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Clinton appropriate a total sum of $3,320,000 for the cost of various capital improvement projects in the Town of Clinton (the “Town”) including: (a) $195,000 for the purchase of a wheeled excavator for the Town’s Department of Public Works (b) $125,000 for the purchase of a generator for the Town’s Police Department (c) $1,000,000 for roads and sidewalks throughout the Town, and (d) $2,000,000 for renovations in the Town library, including, all surveys, alterations, repairs and improvements in connection therewith and engineering, architectural and temporary and permanent financing costs related thereto, and authorize the issuance of bonds and notes or other obligations in the total amount of $3,320,000 to finance such appropriation?"

Coventry.QN:
1.  "Shall Sections 9-3(a) and 9-3(e), which are proposed to be renumbered as 7-3(a)
and 7-3(d), be amended to adjust the threshold at which authorizations for appropriations, bonds or notes must be approved at a town meeting and/or referendum from a fixed dollar amount to a percentage of the current tax levy?"

2.  "Shall additional provisions of the Coventry Town Charter be amended other than
as provided in Question One above, all as recommended in the final report of the Charter
Revision Commission dated July 29, 2026 and as on file with the Coventry Town Clerk?"

Danbury.QN: 1.  "Shall the Charter of the City of Danbury be revised, as recommended by the Charter Revision Commission and approved by the City Council, to provide that the terms of office for all municipal elected offices, including Mayor, Town Clerk, Treasurer, City Council, Zoning Commission, Zoning Commission Alternates, and Constable, upon the municipal election to be held November 2027, be four (4) years, and to provide that the terms of office for all Board of Education members be revised according to Section 2.2.A(c)(1) of the proposed revised Charter of the City of Danbury?"

2.  "Shall all other proposed revisions to the Charter of the City of Danbury, as recommended by the Charter Revision Commission and approved by the City Council, as published, posted on the website of the City of Danbury, and further described in the explanatory text issued by the Town Clerk, be approved?"

Durham.QN: 1.  "Shall the Durham Town Charter be amended to increase the number of members of the Board of Selectmen from three to five?"
2.  "Shall the Durham Town Charter be amended to change the positions of Town Clerk and Tax Collector from elected positions to appointed positions?"

3.  "Shall additional provisions of the Durham Town Charter be amended other than as provided in questions #1 and #2 above, all as recommended in the final report of the Charter Revision Commission dated August 5, 2026, as subsequently amended by the Board of Selectmen on August 24, 2026, and as on file with the Durham Town Clerk?"

Enfield.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Enfield appropriate $511,000,000 for the new construction of Hazardville Memorial Elementary School, Prudence Crandall Elementary School, Parkman Elementary School and Barnard Elementary School and for the conversion of Eli Whitney Elementary School into the Eagle Academy Therapeutic Day School, and authorize the issuance of bonds or notes of the Town in an amount not to exceed $89,000,000 with the balance funded by grants and other available funds?"

2.  "Shall the Enfield Town Charter be revised as proposed by the Charter Revision Commission and as approved by the Enfield Town Council by Resolution #7549 at its special meeting of June, 23, 2026?"

Harwinton.QN: 1.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $5,000,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for HVAC replacements and improvements at district schools?"

2.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $14,935,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for roof replacements and improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School, Lake Garda School and Har-Bur Middle School?"

3.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $3,900,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for the installation of a multipurpose synthetic turf field and related improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School?"

4.  "Shall Regional School District Number 10 appropriate $3,100,000 and authorize bonds and temporary notes in the same amount for the installation of a multipurpose engineered natural grass field and related improvements at Lewis S. Mills High School?"

Middletown.QN: 1.  ""Shall the $30,426,000 appropriation and bond authorization for the Middletown Public Schools Districtwide Infrastructure Project be approved?""

New Canaan.QN: 1.  "Shall the current Charter be changed to require all elected and appointed town officers with managerial authority to comply with applicable Town policies, ethics standards, and lawful administrative directives, and to be accountable to the First Selectman for administrative and operational matters that would not otherwise conflict with their statutory authority?"
2.  "Shall the current Charter be changed to require Town Council confirmation of appointment to the Planning and Zoning Commission?"
3.  "Shall the current Charter be changed to require Town Council approval for changes to Town-owned real property?"
4.  "Shall the current Chater be changed to no longer require Board of Finance members to be real property taxpayers?"
5.  "Shall the current Charter be changed to add 3 alternate members to the Ethics Board?"
6.  "Shall the current Charter be changed to clarify definitions, delete outdated references, and update provisions to current practice?"

Newington.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Newington Appropriate $7,800,000 for the construction of a new Fire Station #4 located at 84 Fifth Street and authorize the issuance of general obligation bonds or notes of the town in an amount not to exceed $7,800,000 to finance the appropriation, or so much as may be necessary after deducting grants to be received for the project?"

Norwich.QN: 1.  ""Shall the $55,000,000 appropriation and bond authorization ordinance for the planning, acquisition and construction of the City of Norwich Police Headquarters Facility Project located at 300 Main Street (Downtown) be approved?""

Oxford.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Oxford adopt the proposed 2026 Charter Revision as approved in accordance with Title 7, Chapter 99 of the Connecticut General Statutes?"

Plainfield.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town Charter be revised to expand the Board of Selectmen from three to five members, effective with the November 2027 town election?"

2.  "Shall the Town Charter be revised to grant the Board of Police Commissioners the authority, upon majority vote, to retain independent legal counsel separate from Town Counsel whenever the Commission determines such representation is necessary to carry out its statutory, disciplinary, investigatory, administrative, or oversight responsibilities, including matters involving conflicts of interest?"
3.  "Shall Charter Section 2-5(d) be revised to raise the grant-match approval limit from $10,000 to $35,000?"
4.  "Shall the Town Charter be revised to require that funds received by the Town under an awarded grant be used only for the purpose stated in that grant?"

Simsbury.QN: 1.  "Shall the Charter of the Township of the Town of Simsbury be amended as proposed by the Simsbury Charter Revision Commission to take effect December 7, 2026 as approved by the Simsbury Board of Selectmen?"

South Windsor.QN:
1.  "Shall the resolution appropriating and authorizing bonds in the amount of $15,000,000 for the planning, design, construction and/or replacement of Town-wide
Road Paving, Traffic Signals, Safety Devices, Culverts, Sidewalks And Drainage
Improvements be approved?"

Southington.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Southington appropriate $86,675,560 for costs related to the Elementary Facilities Plan, including a new Kelley Elementary School, a fit out of the South End Elementary School, and closing Flanders Elementary School and repurposing the building and property for municipal and community use, and authorize the issue of $86,675,560 bonds and notes to finance the appropriation?"

Tolland.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Tolland appropriate $6,500,000 for roof improvements and artificial turf field replacement at Tolland High School and authorize the issuance of general obligation bonds and notes in the same amount to finance said appropriation?"

West Haven.QN: 1.  "Shall the Charter be revised to create a four-year term for Mayor and Town and City Clerk starting in the 2027 municipal election (Art. II 2(c)(1)?"

2.  "Shall the Charter be revised to replace Chapter XX, "Village Improvement Association", also known as the "VIA" with clearer provisions governing the public library's operation by a third-party non-profit (the "VIA"), including its responsibilities, budget obligations, and accountability standards owed to the City (Art.VII, ss10)?"

3.  "Shall the City Charter be updated to make city government clearer, more efficient, and more accountable (the changes would clarify the roles and powers of the Mayor, City Council, departments, boards, and commissons, enhance ethical and financial oversight, strengthen management of city boards and departments, and include other recommendations approved by the Charter Revision Commission and the City Council)?"

Weston.QN: 1.  "Shall the Charter be revised to change the limitation on majority party representation on Boards and Commission from a bare majority to the maximum number permitted under State law (C.G.S. 9-167a) (Art. 1, 1.8)?"

2.  "Shall the Charter be amended to eliminate the ability of the Annual Town Budget Meeting to reduce or eliminate any item in the budget prior to the budget going directly to referendum for approval or disapproval by the voters (Art.9, 9.5)?"

3.  "Shall the remaining proposed Charter amendments contained in the Final Report of the Charter Revision Commission, dated July 13, 2026, as approved by the Board of Selectmen on July 23, 2026, be approved?"

Wethersfield.QN: 1.  "Shall the Town of Wethersfield appropriate $4,000,000 for the purchase of a ladder truck and a rescue truck for the Wethersfield Fire Department and authorize the issuance of bonds or notes of the Town in an amount not to exceed $4,000,000 to finance the appropriation?"

Winchester.QN: 1.  "Shall the Charter be amended to make the Town Clerk position professionally appointed by the Town Manager, effective January 3, 2028?"
2.  "Shall the Charter be amended to extend the term of Registrar of Voters to four years, effective January 3, 2029?"

3.  "Shall the Charter be amended to limit an elector's membership to only one of the following boards: Board of Selectmen; Board of Education; Zoning Board of Appeals; Inland Wetlands and Watercourses Commission; Board of Assessment Appeals; Water and Sewer Commission; Planning and Zoning Commission?"
4.  "Shall the Charter be amended to compress the time frame of the Budget adoption process?"

5.  "Shall the Charter be amended to adopt a definition of elector and property owner and be amended to only allow electors to hold elective office or to serve on any Town board, commission, agency or committee of the Town?"
